- Session opening-range breakouts on DAX, FX and silver: failed.
- Volatility-managed exposure (panel): Sharpe 2.83 / 2.98 against 2.93.
- Gold-silver lead-lag: below cost.
- FX relative strength: intraday, none found. In the literature, momentum on major currencies lost money after 2000 (Menkhoff et al. 2012).

EXCLUDED ON STRUCTURE:
- G10 carry: in-sample rate gaps were tiny, and the cost model ignores swap credits.
- Dollar carry: it was short USD into the 2014-15 USD rally.
- Oil predicting stocks (Driesprong et al.): the oil-stock correlation turned positive after 2008.
- Month-end pension rebalancing and options-expiry weeks: 12 or fewer independent dates a year.
- Crypto cross-sectional momentum: alt-coin CFDs cost 15 bp or more, longs pay 20 %/yr swap, and only 2019-2021 is in sample.

ARITHMETIC THAT DRIVES THE PRIORS. t >= 2.5 over nine in-sample years requires an annual Sharpe of at least 0.83 for the sleeve. Slow premia (trend, calendar cycles) rarely reach that, so their in-sample odds are low by construction.

RANKING. Expected value = P(in sample) x P(validation | in sample):
1. G10 FX weekend overreaction: 12 % x 30 % (data on disk).
2. EM FX weekend overreaction: 10 % x 25 % (needs data).
3. FOMC-cycle long-short: 9 % x 20 % (on disk).
4. Weekly 12-1 time-series momentum: 5 % x 25 % (on disk).
5. Treasury-auction concession: 5 % x 20 % (needs data; FP's US10YR only exists since Dec 2021).
6. JP225 Tokyo-session short: 4 % x 20 % (in-sample data on disk).
7. Pre-holiday basket: 4 % x 15 % (on disk).
All seven together are worth about 0.1 new validated sleeve. Hypotheses 1 and 2 share a mechanism.

Honest reading: the pool of documented anomalies on FP's cheap instruments is close to exhausted. Breadth from this pool can add at most a couple of sleeves and cannot close the 4-5x gap. Suggested order: run 1, then 3 and 4 (cheap, on disk), then 7 and 6, and only then 2 and 5 (both need data).

hypotheses.name: FX weekend overreaction fade (G10 pairs)
hypotheses.family: Liquidity overreaction / calendar: weekend-gap reversal
hypotheses.instruments: eurusd, gbpusd, usdjpy, audusd, usdcad, usdchf, nzdusd, eurjpy (judged as one basket)
hypotheses.rule:
CLOCK: New York time, DST-aware (FP server = NY + 7 h).

SIGNAL:
- F = mid at the open of the first M1 bar at or after Friday 16:50 NY.
- Decision time D = Sunday 20:00 NY (Monday 03:00 server, Tokyo open). P = mid at the open of the first M1 bar at or after D; skip the pair if there is no bar within 15 min.
- sigma = standard deviation of the pair's last 60 daily log returns (days ending 17:00 NY).
- z = ln(P/F) / sigma.
- Signal when |z| is at or above the 75th percentile of that pair's |z| over its previous 104 weekends (at least 52 weekends of history required).
- Side = -sign(z): fade the weekend move.

ENTRY: market at D.
STOP: 1.0 x ATR(20) of daily bars, from the fill.
EXIT: market at Wednesday 12:00 NY, before the Wednesday 17:00 NY triple swap (hold of 64 h at most). No profit target.
SIZING: 1 R = stop distance; equal R per pair; one position per pair. Research evaluates every signal; the hands' position cap is applied afterwards.

JUDGED as a basket under PROTOCOL_V3 s.4: t on daily sums >= 2.5, pooled PF >= 1.12, at least 65 % of pairs positive, no pair above 25 % of the profit.

DECLARED NEIGHBOURS: percentile 65 or 85; fixed threshold |z| >= 0.4; exit Monday 16:00, Tuesday 12:00 or Friday 12:00 NY; profit target at F; decision at 19:00 or 21:00 NY.

NULL: the same clock time on randomly drawn weekends, with the same side mix, stop distances and durations.
hypotheses.rationale:
Weekend news, stop orders left resting over the weekend, and risk-limit orders all execute at the Sunday reopen. At that hour only Wellington and Sydney dealers quote, so the book is the thinnest of the week: the move overshoots, and part of it comes back as Tokyo and then London liquidity arrive.

The payer is whoever is forced, by a stop or a risk limit, to trade in those hours. The edge is a liquidity premium, not a forecast, and the weekend closure that creates it is structural.

This is also the lab's only currency idea with a horizon of several days. The FX ideas that failed earlier were intraday edges of 1-2 bp against about 1 bp of cost. A reversion over 2-3 days can be several times FP's 0.6-1.9 bp round-trip cost.

PUBLISHED: Dao, McGroarty and Urquhart (2016), 'A calendar effect: weekend overreaction (and subsequent reversal) in spot FX rates', Journal of Multinational Financial Management 37-38: 158-167.

- After a large difference between the Friday close and the Monday open, prices tend to reverse over several horizons during the following week. Summaries report only one of 16 pairs without a significant reversal.
- Their reversal strategy is reported as robust to transaction costs and interest rates, with abnormal risk-adjusted returns out of sample.
- Caveat: I could read only the abstract and summaries; the full text was unreachable from this session, so their sample span and gap threshold are unverified.

AFTER PUBLICATION: I found no replication. The lab's 2013-2021 window lies mostly after their data, so the in-sample test doubles as an out-of-sample check, and the validation years are entirely post-publication.

RELATED LAB EVIDENCE: the round-1 gold weekend-gap fade failed (meanrev #14: n 99, PF 0.87; fading gap-ups PF 1.31, fading gap-downs 0.30). hypotheses.name: FOMC-cycle even/odd weeks, long-short on US500
hypotheses.family: Calendar / central-bank news risk premium (FOMC cycle)
hypotheses.instruments: us500 primary; declared basket check with ger40; us30 reported as information
hypotheses.rule:
CALENDAR:
- Day 0 = each scheduled FOMC statement day, from the FOMC list in /home/user/gold-orb/lab/tracks/seasonality/calendars.py. The 2020 unscheduled actions are ignored.
- t = NYSE trading days relative to day 0.
- Weeks of the cycle, as in Cieslak-Morse-Vissing-Jorgensen: W0 = t in [-1,+3], W1 = [4,8], W2 = [9,13], W3 = [14,18], W4 = [19,23], W5 = [24,28], W6 = [29,33].
- The five days [-6,-2] before the next day 0 form W-1 and override any later week of the current cycle. Days past 33 are ignored.

POSITION: LONG in W0, W2, W4, W6; SHORT in W1, W3, W5; flat in W-1.
ENTRY: open of the first M1 bar at or after 15:55 NY on the trading day before the week's first day.
EXIT: 15:55 NY on the week's last day. For consecutive weeks, exit and re-enter at the same minute.
STOP: disaster stop at 3 x ATR(20) of daily bars, from the fill.
SIZING: 1 R = stop distance.

ger40 is traded on the same calendar and clock (15:55 NY = 21:55 Berlin, CFD still open).

DECLARED NEIGHBOURS: entry and exit at 15:30 NY; week boundaries shifted by +1 trading day; stop at 2 or 4 ATR; W-1 short instead of flat. Long-only even weeks are a diagnostic only.

NULL: calendar rule, same trades at random moments.
hypotheses.rationale:
News from the Fed arrives every other week (Board meetings and the informal communication that follows them). Equity investors therefore demand a premium to hold risk through the even weeks of the FOMC cycle and earn nothing in odd weeks. It is a risk premium, paid by those who cut equity exposure ahead of possible Fed news, not a mispricing.

The short leg in odd weeks makes the rule nearly beta-neutral over a cycle, so it cannot pass merely because the market rose (the lab's null test). Shorts carry no swap in the FP cost model, so that leg is cheap. It adds a weekly clock on the US index that the ten do not use.
hypotheses.evidence:
PUBLISHED: Cieslak, Morse and Vissing-Jorgensen, 'Stock returns over the FOMC cycle', Journal of Finance 74(5), 2019, 2201-2248. Working-paper figures for 1994-2013 (more than 160 meetings):
- Average 5-day excess return: +0.57 % in week 0, +0.30 % week 2, +0.42 % week 4, +0.61 % week 6.
- Odd weeks: about 0 in week -1, -0.17 % week 1, -0.17 % week 3, -0.12 % week 5.
- Daily regression: +13.6 bp a day in week 0 and +10 bp a day in weeks 2/4/6 above odd weeks, both significant at 1 %.
- Holds in 1994-2000, 2001-2007 and 2008-2013, and in MSCI developed-ex-US and emerging indices (emerging +18 bp a day, t 4.75).

AFTER PUBLICATION: I found no replication after 2016. The journal version notes that the Lucca-Moench pre-FOMC drift, which sits inside week 0, is not significant in post-publication data. The lab measured it at +6.2 bp (t 0.98) on us500 in 2013-2021, against about 49 bp in 1994-2011 (/home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/r2/events/desc3_windows.txt). Week 0 has therefore largely decayed; weeks 2/4/6 have not been tested after 2013.

hypotheses.name: Treasury auction concession on FP's US 10-year note CFD
hypotheses.family: Supply pressure / dealer inventory (auction cycle)
hypotheses.instruments: FP US10YR (CFD on CME 10-year T-note futures); FP GILT as a separate, later check
hypotheses.rule:
CALENDAR: US nominal coupon auctions of 5-, 7-, 10-, 20- and 30-year securities (results at 13:00 NY). Auctions on consecutive business days form one cluster [C1, C2], about three clusters a month.

SHORT LEG: sell at 15:00 NY (futures settlement) three business days before C1; buy back at 13:05 NY on C2.
LONG LEG: buy at 13:05 NY on C2; sell at 15:00 NY two business days later.
STOP: 2 x ATR(20) of daily bars, from the fill.
SIZING: 1 R = stop distance. No filter.

DECLARED NEIGHBOURS: short from T-5 or T-2; long exit at T+1 or T+3; 10- and 30-year auctions only; skip legs that contain an FOMC statement or an NFP/CPI release.

NULL: calendar rule, same legs at random dates.
hypotheses.rationale: Dealers must absorb a large, pre-announced supply with limited balance sheets. They cheapen or short the outstanding issues before the auction and are paid by the recovery after it. The payer is the issuer, and the end-investors, through that concession. Rates are a market and a calendar that the ten never touch.
hypotheses.evidence:
PUBLISHED:
- Lou, Yan and Zhang (2013), Review of Financial Studies 26(8), 1980-2008: secondary prices fall in the days before auctions and recover afterwards. Example: before the next 2-year auction, the 2-year note is 8.89 bp (t 2.93) below its 5-day post-auction return. Issuance cost 9-18 bp of auction size.
- Fleming, Liu and Nguyen (NY Fed Staff Report 1188, March 2026, revised October 2026; intraday data 1991-2024): yields rise in the hours before an auction and reverse afterwards, by 0.7-1.2 bp in total across maturities.
- Beetsma et al. (2016, 2018): a similar V-shape in euro-area government bonds.

AFTER PUBLICATION:
- Fleming, Liu and Nguyen measure a 0.75 bp decline from 2007-2014 to 2015-2024, as investment funds absorb more of the supply.
- Somogyi, Wallen and Xu (2025-26): since 2010, US yields no longer tend to fall over auctions.
The decay is measured and substantial.

FP's US10YR spread has not been read. One CME tick (1/64 = 0.0156) is about 1.4 bp of price at 111. At 2 ticks plus slippage, about 3 bp per round trip. No swap: it is a futures-based CFD with a roll adjustment instead.

hypotheses.family: Overnight-versus-intraday return decomposition
hypotheses.instruments: jp225
hypotheses.rule:
DAYS: every Tokyo exchange trading day (python holidays JP, plus 31 December to 3 January).

ENTRY: sell at the open of the first M1 bar at or after 09:05 Tokyo (00:05 UTC; Japan has no DST).
EXIT: buy back at the open of the first M1 bar at or after 14:55 Tokyo up to 2024-11-04, and 15:25 Tokyo from 2024-11-05 (the TSE close moved from 15:00 to 15:30 that day).

hypotheses.name: ger40_noise30_xetra: the us100 noise-area rule, frozen, on the DAX's own cash clock
hypotheses.family: session momentum from the cash open (noise area); frozen transfer to a new market's own clock
hypotheses.instruments: GER40 (FP Markets cash CFD on the DAX, EUR; lab frame lab/data/fp/ger40_m1.parquet)
hypotheses.rule: Clock Europe/Berlin (DST from tz data). Days: Xetra full trading days from 2014-01-01. Skip 24 and 31 Dec (early closes) and the day after an early close. Prices are mid (bid+ask)/2. 'Price at T' = close of the M1 bar that starts at T−1 min. Skip a check if the last quote is older than 10 min. O = open of the 09:00 bar. PC = close of the previous Xetra session's 17:29 bar. Checks at T = 09:30, 10:00, …, 17:00 (16 checks). sigma(T) = mean over the previous 14 sessions (at least 9 with data) of |P_d(T)/O_d − 1|. UB = max(O,PC)·(1+sigma(T)); LB = min(O,PC)·(1−sigma(T)). State machine identical to noise30: if flat and P(T) > UB, buy at market with stop-loss at max(O,PC); if flat and P(T) < LB, sell at market with stop-loss at min(O,PC); if long and P(T) < UB, or short and P(T) > LB, close at market and go flat. After a stop-loss the state stays long/short (no re-entry) until a check passes the exit test. Close everything at 17:25:00. One position at most. Sizing: fixed % of equity risked per trade, R = |fill − stop|. Declared neighbours: lookback 11/17; band multiplier 0.8/1.2; check step 15/60 min; first check 09:15/09:45; exit 17:15/17:29. Null: the lab's mode 'day' (same Berlin time on a random day, same side, stop and hold).
hypotheses.rationale: The cash open concentrates orders accumulated overnight that institutions execute through the session: VWAP/TWAP programmes, index and ETF flows, gamma hedging by option and leveraged-ETF dealers. A move out of the time-of-day 'noise area' signals an imbalance whose remaining slices are still to come. The other side is liquidity takers who must finish their programmes today whatever the price. This is the only session mechanism the lab has validated out of sample (noise30 on us100), and it has never run on the DAX's own clock. Prior 25 % for validation, because the identical rule held on us100 in 2022–25 (PF 1.227, 4/4 years). Against that: the us100 validation profit was almost all longs (+47.5 R vs +1.1 R), and the DAX's own momentum measured from the previous close failed validation (late_mom_1600: IS t 3.49, VAL PF 0.977). My odds of passing in sample: about 30 %, partly because the family is known to look good in sample on the DAX.
hypotheses.evidence: Lab: noise30 on us100: IS n 1643, PF 1.30, t 3.28, 8/8 years; VAL n 850, PF 1.227, t 1.97, 4/4 years (results/r2/recalc/summary.json via the archivist). DAX momentum measured from the previous 17:30 close at 30-minute marks 09:30–16:30 (|z| ≥ 1.5): IS n 665, PF 1.420, t 3.27, 8/9 years, but long +146.5 R vs short +22.1 R. Published: Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon (2024, SSRN, 'Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)'), the source of the noise rule. Baltussen, Da, Lammers and Martens (2021, Journal of Financial Economics, 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum') find intraday momentum across 60+ futures, including non-US equity indices, and tie it to gamma hedging.

hypotheses.name: us500_expiry_pin: S&P 500 pulled toward the nearest 25-point strike on PM-expiry afternoons
hypotheses.family: options-expiry microstructure (delta-hedging pin) at the US cash close
hypotheses.instruments: US500 (FP Markets cash CFD on the S&P 500; lab/data/fp/us500_m1.parquet)
hypotheses.rule: Clock America/New_York. Rule days are S&P 500 PM-settled expiry days with a full NYSE session: every Friday; Wednesdays from the listing of Wednesday SPX Weeklys (about Feb 2016); Mondays from the listing of Monday Weeklys (about Aug 2016); and the last business day of each month. The two listing dates are to be confirmed from Cboe notices. Skip early closes and holidays, and skip a Thursday expiry that precedes a Friday holiday. At 14:00:00: P = mid close of the 13:59 bar; K = 25 × round(P/25), the nearest multiple of 25 index points; D = K − P. If |D| ≥ 5 points: market order toward K (buy if D > 0, sell if D < 0). Take-profit limit at K. Stop-loss at the mirror point P − D, so R = |D| and the target is +1 R. Otherwise close at market at 15:58:00. One trade per day. Sizing: fixed % risk per trade. Mechanism control declared now: the same rule on Tuesdays and Thursdays from Sep 2016 to Dec 2021 that are not month-ends, when no PM S&P 500 expiry existed. Expiry-day mean R minus placebo mean R must be > 0 with t ≥ 2. Declared neighbours: decision 13:30/14:30; grid 10/50 points; minimum distance 3/8 points; exit 15:50/15:59. Pre-check, not a trial: the frame's 16:00 price must match the official S&P 500 close within ±1 point on at least 90 % of in-sample days. Otherwise shift the grid each day by the previous day's (frame 16:00 − official close), known before 14:00.
hypotheses.rationale: On expiry afternoons, market makers who are long gamma at heavily traded strikes must sell above the strike and buy below it to stay delta-neutral. That pulls the index toward the strike into the 16:00 settlement. The hedging is forced and price-insensitive; the losers are momentum traders and holders of the expiring options. There are many trades because SPX has had three weekly PM expiries since 2016, and Tuesdays/Thursdays, with no expiry before 2022, give a clean placebo. Prior 15 % for validation: the effect's sign depends on whether dealers are net long or short gamma, and daily 0DTE options from 2022 changed that landscape. My odds of passing in sample: about 8 %.
hypotheses.evidence: Ni, Pearson and Poteshman (2005, Journal of Financial Economics, 'Stock price clustering on option expiration dates'): optionable stocks close near strikes on expiry Fridays, linked to market makers' delta hedging. Golez and Jackwerth (2012, Journal of Financial Economics, 'Pinning in the S&P 500 futures'): S&P 500 futures pulled toward option strikes on expiry days. Ni, Pearson, Poteshman and White (2021, Review of Financial Studies): when hedgers are net short gamma, prices are pushed away instead. No lab evidence on indices. On gold, round numbers break through rather than attract (results/pivots/report.md: z −4.5 to −5.5), but spot gold has no listed-option pin.

Cross-asset and regime. What the record shows: lead-lag between the robot's markets at the minute scale costs more than it earns everywhere except us100 -> BTC. hypotheses.name: IDXRS_1000: US index relative-strength pair, 10:00 to 15:55 New York
hypotheses.family: dispersion / relative value (two-legged, market-neutral index pair, intraday)
hypotheses.instruments: us100, us500, us30 (FP cash CFDs); each day one pair = strongest and weakest of the three
hypotheses.rule: Clock: New York (DST-aware), NYSE regular sessions Mon-Fri, early-close days skipped. Prices: mid = (bid+ask)/2 of M1 bars. SIGNAL at 10:00: for i in {us100, us500, us30}, r_i = ln(mid close of the 09:59 bar / mid open of the 09:30 bar); z_i = r_i / sd(r_i over the previous 60 sessions). S = argmax z_i, W = argmin z_i, D = z_S - z_W. Trade only if D >= the 75th percentile of D over the previous 60 sessions (at least 40 values). Hedge ratio h = sd_S/sd_W, where sd = sd of each index's 10:00->15:55 log return over the previous 60 sessions. ENTRY at the open of the 10:00 M1 bar: market BUY S (notional N) and market SELL W (notional h*N) in the same minute; if one leg fails, close the other at once. Pair mark pi(t) = ln(P_S(t)/P_S,fill) - h*ln(P_W(t)/P_W,fill) at exit-side prices, in bp of N. STOP: close both legs at market when pi <= -1.5*sd_pi, where sd_pi = sd over the previous 60 sessions of the 10:00->15:55 mid pi of the pair the same ranking picked each day (traded or not). EXIT: both legs at the open of the 15:55 bar. One pair per day (every signal is taken). SIZING: 1 R = 1.5*sd_pi*N in money; N from the risk budget, rounded down to the lot step on both legs; the day is skipped if a leg is below the broker minimum (Addendum E). R per trade = net pi / (1.5*sd_pi). Neighbours, declared before the run: entry 09:55 / 10:15; threshold Q67 / Q80; windows 40 / 80 sessions; stop 1.25 / 1.75; ranking on raw returns instead of z; exit 15:30 / 15:59; fixed pair us100-us500.
hypotheses.rationale: Style and sector rotation (Nasdaq-100 technology against the Dow's industrials and financials) is decided at the open, on overnight news and the earnings of a few index heavyweights. Large allocators then execute it through the session with participation/VWAP algorithms. Nasdaq-100 products (QQQ, NQ, TQQQ/SQQQ, QQQ options) also carry their own hedging demand, which the Dow products lack. Who loses: liquidity providers who keep absorbing one-sided flow, and slow allocators who rebalance the same day. Long one index and short another, volatility-hedged, the bet removes the market direction, which the null test controls and which ocm4/noise30 already hold. P(IS pass) about 40 %: the top-quartile descriptive edge nets out at t about 2.5 after two legs of cost.

ranking.rule:
CLOCK AND DAYS: New York (DST-aware), NYSE full sessions; early closes skipped. Mid = (bid+ask)/2 of M1 bars.

SIGNAL at 10:00:
- For us100, us500 and us30: r_i = ln(mid close of the 09:59 bar / mid open of the 09:30 bar).
- RAW returns, as in r2/tracks/leadlag/desc_rs.py. The team's z-ranking is not used: it adds a free choice, and it adds us500-against-us30 days, whose per-leg results were negative.
- S = argmax r, W = argmin r, D = r_S - r_W.
- Trade only if D >= the 75th percentile of D over the previous 60 sessions (at least 40 values).

HEDGE: h = sd_S / sd_W, where sd = standard deviation of each index's 10:00->15:55 log return over the previous 60 sessions.

ENTRY at the open of the 10:00 M1 bar: market BUY S (notional N) and market SELL W (notional h x N) in the same minute. If one leg fails, close the other at once.

PAIR MARK: pi = ln(P_S/P_S,fill) - h x ln(P_W/P_W,fill), at exit-side prices.

STOP: close both legs at market when pi <= -1.5 x sd_pi. sd_pi = sd over the previous 60 sessions of the hedged 10:00->15:55 mid return of the pair the same ranking picked each day, traded or not.

EXIT: both legs at the open of the 15:55 bar. One pair a day; every signal is taken.

SIZING: 1 R = 1.5 x sd_pi x N; R = net pi / (1.5 x sd_pi). On the account, a signal whose two legs cannot both be placed at the broker's minimum lot within 1.5 % risk is skipped (Addendum E).

ranking.rule:
CLOCK AND DAYS: Europe/Berlin (DST from tz data). Xetra full trading days; skip 24 and 31 December and the day after an early close.

PRICES: mid. 'Price at T' = close of the M1 bar that starts at T-1 min. A check is skipped if the last quote is older than 10 min.

ANCHORS: O = open of the 09:00 bar. PC = close of the previous Xetra session's 17:29 bar.

CHECKS at T = 09:30, 10:00, ..., 17:00 (16 checks).
- sigma(T) = mean over the previous 14 sessions (at least 9 with data) of |P_d(T)/O_d - 1|.
- UB = max(O,PC) x (1 + sigma(T)); LB = min(O,PC) x (1 - sigma(T)).

STATE MACHINE, identical to noise30:
- flat and P(T) > UB: buy at market, stop at max(O,PC);
- flat and P(T) < LB: sell at market, stop at min(O,PC);
- long and P(T) < UB, or short and P(T) > LB: close at market.
- After a stop the state stays long or short (no re-entry) until a check passes the exit test.

EXIT: close everything at 17:25:00. One position at most.

SIZING: 1 R = |fill - stop|.

PARAMETERS: frozen from noise30 on us100 (lookback 14, band multiplier 1.0, step 30 min; results/r2/recalc/summary.json). Nothing is tuned on the DAX.

rejected.reason: The rule changes meaning in validation: SPX Tuesday and Thursday PM expiries were listed in 2022, so every weekday becomes a rule day and the declared Tuesday/Thursday placebo disappears. Whether price pins or is pushed away depends on dealers' net gamma, which broker data cannot see (Ni, Pearson, Poteshman and White 2021). It needs the strike to be hit before the mirror stop on about 56 % of trades, against about 50 % for a driftless walk. Re-aligning the grid when the CFD-index basis drifts needs official index closes, which is an outside feed. Probability of passing validation about 0.5 %.

LIKELY OUTCOME: about 0.18 sleeves expected to pass validation from the five picks (8.8 + 2.8 + 3.3 + 1.5 + 1.6 %).
- None passes: about 83 %.
- Exactly one passes: about 16 %.
- Two or more pass: about 1 %.
The most likely single pass is IDXRS_1000. It counts as breadth only if its correlation with the us100 sleeves stays under the declared 0.30.

WHERE THE ACCOUNT STANDS (my computation from results/r2/recalc/trades: weekly sums of R at 1 R per trade, 2022-2025):
- The ten make +2.05 R a week with a weekly sd of 7.32 R: an annualised Sharpe of 2.02 over 209 weeks (2.86 on 2018-02 to 2021).
- They behave like 3 nearly independent clusters: us100 1.43, crypto 1.16, gold 1.04 (correlations between clusters -0.09 to +0.04; sqrt(1.43^2 + 1.16^2 + 1.04^2) = 2.11).
- Single sleeves range from 0.52 to 1.26.
- The ten kept 29-119 % of their in-sample Sharpe (median about 62 %), so a newcomer that passes should be worth s of about 0.6.

BREADTH ARITHMETIC: a sleeve of Sharpe s with correlation c to the account raises the account's Sharpe squared by (s - 2.02c)^2/(1 - c^2) at best weighting.
- s 0.6, c 0: 2.02 -> 2.11 (+4 %).
- s 0.6, c 0.1: 2.02 -> 2.06 (+2 %).
- c 0.3: no gain. A newcomer must beat 2.02 x c to add anything, which is why independence matters more than trade count.
- Two independent passes: 2.19 (+8 %).
- All five passing (about 2 in 100 million): about 2.25 (+12 %).
- Expected value of this round: about +0.4 % of account Sharpe.
- At equal weekly swing, +2 % of Sharpe is about +0.04 R a week (2.05 -> 2.09), about +2 R a year on today's +107 R.

AGAINST THE USER'S DEMAND: the gap is about x4.4 (PROTOCOL_V3, Addendum I outcome), a Sharpe near 8.9.
- That needs about 75 more units of Sharpe squared: about 210 new independent sleeves of 0.6, or 75 of 1.0, or 50 more clusters like today's.
- The lab found 3 clusters in about 2,300 logged configurations.
- Breadth from this pool can add a few percent and settle four open questions: FX weekends, the DAX's own clock, index relative value, the FOMC cycle.
- It cannot deliver 'x2 a month with 10-20 % falls'. At a 5 % stake the typical month stays near +12 %, with a fall of 20 % or more in about 58 % of months (results/r2/stake/x2/x2.json). A typical +100 % month with rare 20 % falls needs every trade's edge x4-5 (results/r2/stake/x2/x2b.json).
